history.text: Portuguese navigators reached the Kongo coast and opened four centuries of contact.
Luanda became a principal Atlantic slave-trading port.
An armed independence struggle was fought against Portuguese rule.
Independence was declared on 11 November as Portuguese rule ended.
A long civil war followed, ending with a ceasefire in 2002.
A new constitution set the framework of the current republic.

worthSeeing.title: Kalandula Falls:
worthSeeing.text: One of Africa's largest waterfalls by volume, on the Lucala River in Malanje.

worthSeeing.title: Fortress of Sao Miguel:
worthSeeing.text: The 1576 Portuguese fort above Luanda, now the armed forces museum.

worthSeeing.title: Tundavala Gap:
worthSeeing.text: An escarpment viewpoint near Lubango where the plateau drops sharply to the plain.
